faq.question: Which New College is this?
faq.answer: This is The New College on Peters Road in Royapettah, Chennai, established in 1951 and affiliated to the University of Madras. The adjacent MEASI architecture, management and information-technology institutions have separate identities; their programmes are not automatically New College offerings.

faq.question: Who can apply to undergraduate programmes?
faq.answer: The college’s admission policy restricts undergraduate admission to men. Applicants must meet the exact programme’s Higher Secondary subject requirements and the college’s selection and original-document checks. Recognition or equivalence documentation is required where specified.

faq.question: Can women apply for postgraduate study?
faq.answer: The college states that selected aided and self-financed PG programmes admit women. These entries verify the male applicant route; they do not establish women’s availability for every exact PG degree or claim that women are ineligible. Confirm the selected programme directly.

faq.question: Can international applicants apply?
faq.answer: The admission policy permits eligible applicants from India and abroad. NRI and foreign applicants provide a passport copy; accepted qualification equivalence and University of Madras eligibility checks apply. The college also requires foreign students to hold a regular long-term student visa. Admission and immigration checks remain separate.

faq.question: Which school subjects are needed?
faq.answer: Requirements vary by award. Physics and Mathematics specify science-subject combinations; Chemistry has CPM and CPZ alternatives. Commerce requires Commerce or Business Studies and Accountancy, while Information System Management specifies Computer Science or Computer Applications. Use the exact programme requirements.

faq.question: How do postgraduate qualifications differ?
faq.answer: The current prospectus gives separate degree conditions. Arabic, English and Tamil include named degrees or specified foundation-language study routes; Commerce includes particular Commerce and allied degree combinations. Science programmes require their named degree or another qualification accepted by the University of Madras.

faq.question: What teaching languages are recorded?
faq.answer: The named institutional table records English for the unchanged supported awards, English with Tamil for BA Tamil, English with Urdu for BA Urdu and Tamil for MA Tamil. These are dated programme records with current title continuation; confirm current arrangements. Bilingual listings do not guarantee an English-only section.

faq.question: What intake dates have been verified?
faq.answer: The published 2026–27 academic calendar schedules first-year UG and PG classes and student induction for 1 July 2026. The site lists 31 August 2026 as that cycle’s application deadline. These are dated published schedules, not an independently verified universal actual start or a future admission window.

faq.question: What do the fee amounts include?
faq.answer: The displayed figures use the latest published isolated tuition component. Compulsory college charges, examinations, hostel, meals and living costs are separate. NIL tuition does not mean free study. Confirm your applicable admission quote, including any nationality or category-related charges, before payment.

faq.question: How do applications work?
faq.answer: Register through the official portal, verify your mobile number and email, enter the academic details, pay the application charge and finalise the application. Provisional selection is communicated by SMS and email. Attend the notified interview with the required records and complete verification and payment if selected.

faq.question: Is accommodation included with admission?
faq.answer: Hostel admission is a separate application after college admission. The prospectus describes boys’ accommodation, a separate PG section, prepared meals and water facilities. Confirm eligibility, vacancy, residence rules and the full hostel and mess charge before planning a stay.

faq.answer: The UGC’s own list records autonomy for 2023–24 to 2032–33, and the University of Madras lists the institution as an affiliated aided autonomous college. These institutional statuses do not establish approval for every newly proposed award or professional programme.
